title: BCL-2 Inhibitors in B-Cell Lymphomas Beyond CLL: Biological Rationale, Clinical Evidence, and Future Directions
content: Dysregulation of B-cell lymphoma 2 (BCL-2)-mediated apoptosis contributes to the pathogenesis and treatment resistance of B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphomas (NHLs), providing a rationale for therapeutic targeting of this pathway. However, differences in molecular characteristics and functional apoptotic dependence across lymphoma subtypes result in heterogeneous responses to BCL-2 inhibition. This narrative review critically evaluates the biological rationale, clinical efficacy, and safety of BCL-2 inhibitors in follicular lymphoma (FL), diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL), mantle cell lymphoma (MCL), marginal zone lymphoma (MZL), and Waldenström macroglobulinemia/lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma (WM/LPL), excluding chronic lymphocytic leukemia/small lymphocytic lymphoma. Evidence from prospective clinical trials, conference abstracts, and ongoing studies was synthesized, with emphasis on comparative outcomes, treatment-related toxicity, and emerging therapeutic strategies. Clinical outcomes vary substantially across lymphoma subtypes. In FL, randomized evidence has not demonstrated additional benefit from incorporating venetoclax into established chemoimmunotherapy. In aggressive B-cell lymphoma, the addition of venetoclax to DA-EPOCH-R was associated with increased mortality and inferior overall survival in the randomized double-hit lymphoma cohort. Conversely, the phase III SYMPATICO trial demonstrated improved progression-free survival with ibrutinib–venetoclax in relapsed/refractory MCL, although without a significant overall survival benefit. Preliminary studies in MZL and WM/LPL have shown encouraging activity, but evidence remains predominantly nonrandomized. Next-generation BCL-2 inhibitors, including sonrotoclax and lisaftoclax, are expanding investigational treatment options. Overall, BCL-2 inhibition represents a promising but disease-dependent therapeutic strategy. Biomarker-guided patient selection, optimized combinations, and randomized trials incorporating long-term efficacy and safety outcomes are essential to establish its clinical role across B-cell lymphomas.
